newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS upgrades Trilon long-term debt.
newsitem.headline: DBRS upgrades Trilon long-term debt.

text.p: Dominon Bond Rating Service on Monday said it upgraded the long-term debt and preferred shares of Trilon Financial Corp, while confirming the company's commercial paper.

DBRS upgraded all long-term ratings for Trilon, with the senior debt rating increasing to A (low) from BBB (high). Trilon's cumulative preferred shares were increased to Pfd-2 from Pfd-3 and junior preferred shares moved to Pfd-2 (low) from Pfd-3.
The rating on Trilon's commercial paper was maintained at R-1 (low). All ratings carried a stable trend.

DBRS said all of Trilon's ratings had now been removed from "under review" status under which they were placed last month. The decision to review the ratings came after it was announced that Trilon was in talks with the Royal Bank of Canada to sell it Trilon's 57 percent stake in London Insurance Group.
Trilon later said it would tender its stake to Royal Bank's C$27.50-a-share takeover offer.
Even if the sale does not proceed, DBRS said the ratings upgrades are appropriate because of the "meaningful progress" Trilon has made in recent years.
DBRS said Trilon exceeded expectations in the price it received for London Insurance and that balance sheet strength and flexibility will be improved by the sale.
The rating agency said it is comfortable with Trilon plans to reinvest the proceeds from the sale and that Royal Bank securities received as part of the sale will be a long-term holding.
